entry.title: A small signal when you are talking
entry.summary: For an ordinary conversation, Davies describes a hand on the adult’s shoulder as a way to say, “I have something to tell you.” The adult acknowledges the child and returns to them at a pause.
entry.cue: Your toddler wants to speak while you are in a conversation.
detail: Her example uses the adult’s hand over the child’s hand to show the message has been received. The adult then pauses as soon as it is appropriate to listen.
It takes practice and does not set a length of time a toddler should wait. This is an ordinary conversation signal, not a condition for getting urgent help.

references.section: Learning how to interrupt an adult
references.locator: Shoulder-hand signal, adult acknowledgment and response at appropriate pause

ageContext.bookAge: No fixed age is stated for the toddler conversation signal.
ageContext.readiness: A child wants to communicate during an ordinary adult conversation and can use the shared gesture.
ageContext.note: This is an optional gesture with adult acknowledgment, not a waiting-time expectation or a condition for help. Age and readiness sources: The Montessori Toddler, PDF pp. 14.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
